text: I've created `filter.py`. Run it as `python3 filter.py file.html` and it rewrites the file in place. My test page of ordinary HTML came out byte-for-byte unchanged. About 40 known XSS tricks all came out disarmed, as far as I can tell by reading the output. I didn't check any of it in a real browser. **How it works:** it reads the HTML following the same rules browsers use, and cuts out only the dangerous pieces. Everything else is copied exactly, including whitespace, Windows line endings, entities and bytes that aren't valid text. That's why it uses no parsing library: rebuilding the page from a parse tree would change its formatting. **What it removes:** - `script>…`. **Things that may surprise you:** - Some harmless text is removed too: a `` comment that mentions script, or an attribute like `x/onerror=` that browsers would treat as part of a URL. This was a deliberate choice to keep the output free of obvious attack strings. - ``-style links lose their `href` but keep the link text. - `
